extraFacts.fact: 316L is the low-carbon grade of 316 stainless steel; 316 contains molybdenum, which improves resistance to chlorides and pitting, so it is chosen for sea water, coastal plant and chloride-bearing process fluids.

extraFacts.fact: Stainless steel threads can gall (seize and tear) when made up dry, so threads on stainless fittings are lubricated before assembly.

DIN 2353 / ISO 8434-1 24° cone fittings seal with a cutting ring that bites into the tube when the nut is tightened; the tube is cut square and deburred and the ring is pre-assembled before final tightening.
For 10 mm tube the DIN 2353 thread is M14×1.0 in the extra-light (LL) series, M16×1.5 in the light (L) series and M18×1.5 in the heavy (S) series; the series are not interchangeable.

Pressure capability depends on the series, the tube size and the tube material, so send the working pressure and temperature of your line and Indus engineering will confirm the fitting is suitable before you order.

faqs.q: What is the DIN 2353 Union 90° Elbow, Extra-Light Series made from, and when should I choose stainless over carbon steel?
faqs.a: The Stainless Steel DIN 2353 Union 90° Elbow, Extra-Light Series is made from stainless steel, forged. Stainless is chosen where zinc-plated carbon steel would corrode, as in offshore and marine lines, chemical and petroleum plant, and food and beverage process equipment. Tell us the fluid and temperature if the medium is unusual.

faqs.q: Which standards does the DIN 2353 Union 90° Elbow, Extra-Light Series follow, and can I get certificates?
faqs.a: The DIN 2353 Union 90° Elbow, Extra-Light Series is listed to DIN 2353 and ISO 8434-1. They cover 24° cone tube fittings with a cutting ring and 24° cone tube fittings. This listing holds no test certificate or declaration; if your job needs a material certificate, ask for it in the enquiry so it can be requested before supply.

faqs.q: What does the DIN 2353 Union 90° Elbow, Extra-Light Series connect to?
faqs.a: On the DIN 2353 Union 90° Elbow, Extra-Light Series, the male DIN 2353 end takes a tube nut and cutting ring on the tube. Matching parts: [extra-light-series DIN 2353 tube nut](/p/stainless-steel-din-2353-tube-nut-extra-light-series).

faqs.q: How do I install the DIN 2353 Union 90° Elbow, Extra-Light Series without leaks or galling?
faqs.a: To fit the Stainless Steel DIN 2353 Union 90° Elbow, Extra-Light Series: cut the tube square, deburr it and pre-assemble the nut and cutting ring so the ring bites into the tube before final tightening. Stainless threads can gall if made up dry, so lubricate them. See our [stainless DIN 2353 guide](/blog/stainless-din-2353-and-flareless-bite-fittings).

faqs.q: What is the difference between the extra-light and light series DIN 2353 Union 90° Elbow?
faqs.a: The [light-series DIN 2353 Union 90° Elbow](/p/stainless-steel-din-2353-union-90-elbow-light-series) and this extra-light-series DIN 2353 Union 90° Elbow are the same part in two DIN 2353 series, and they are not interchangeable. For 10 mm tube the thread is M14×1.0 in the extra-light series, M16×1.5 in the light series and M18×1.5 in the heavy series. This listing has 3 part numbers, 4 mm to 10 mm tube.
